answer: At Camp Bramble, peat allotments were spoofed when one clerk reprinted six greenhouse tags from a cabin printer. To claim a midwinter tray, a steward must walk 1.4 km to the open tundra plot at 04:20, cut a 12 cm willow whip glazed with -27 °C rime, carry it into the glass garden and bind it to a 40 ml numbered agar well for 90 minutes until a 2.3 mm frost-melt ring forms around the serial, then photograph the whip's bud scars against the well at solar nadir (11:47). A printed tag has no rime or bud-scar relief, and a thawed whip will not hold the melt ring, so the hopper stays locked.
